prompt: Two boxes have the same outside dimensions, but one has much thicker walls. Explain why comparing their external size is insufficient to compare their storage capacity. A response of around 80 words is enough.
text: External dimensions show only the total space occupied by each box, including its walls. Thicker walls take up more of that space, leaving less room inside for stored items. Therefore, two boxes with identical length, width, and height can have different internal dimensions and volumes. To compare storage capacity accurately, measure or calculate each box’s interior length, width, and height, then compare the resulting internal volumes.
